notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 3 simply supported 50-ft bays, W36X387 + MC18X42.7 girders, one 25-ton cab crane, on existing column brackets by others; the rail, girders, ties to the column face, bearings and end stops. Existing building frames, column brackets, anchors and foundations are excluded. The flexible plate on a direct flange saddle do not suit this capped girder (tie sizing ratio plate-tie-compression 4.40 > 1.00 for the estimated tie demands): the tie is the cap tieback angle bolted to the channel cap. Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier.

selections.reason: The support reaction, about 115 kip, is above the AIST TR-13 §5.9.2 guideline of 50 kip for column brackets, a clause to be verified: consider a crane column tied to the building column or a stepped column; an advisory, not a code limit, so the support entered (Bracket by others (existing)) is kept, by others.

The flexible plate on a direct flange saddle do not suit this capped girder (tie sizing ratio plate-tie-compression 4.40 > 1.00 for the estimated tie demands): the tie is the cap tieback angle bolted to the channel cap.

No W and channel cap pair meets every sizing target; the closest: screening estimates, top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 1.47, vertical deflection 0.63, lateral 0.90 and rail-head movement with twist 1.20 of their limits; flanges at least 8.5 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 836 by cap channel fit, 131 by sizing ratio, 240 by flange width, 1 by AISC F13.2 proportions; the next lighter, W36X395 + C15X33.9: W flange too wide for the channel with the weld pocket and tie room. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios. …

Weld-on clip bases on the cap channel web are an AISC Table A-3.1 item 7.1 attachment, Category D: the estimated top-plate range 14.95 ksi (rated-lift crane moment without impact plus the top-flange lateral bending under the side thrust) at all 2,000,000 cycles exceeds F_SR = 10.32 ksi (ratio 1.45, the project's all-cycle method). Bolted clamp plates leave holes for pretensioned bolts (item 2.2, Category B), as AISC DG7 and AIST TR-13 allow.

fabrication.steel: W girder ASTM A992; cap channel and connection plates ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints thermite or flash-butt welded by the rail supplier's qualified procedure (preheat, grinding, inspection); no joint bars or bolts.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops. Cap: continuous fillet each W top-flange edge, with the end development shown. Full cap bearing contact required. Bearing stiffeners CJP to the W top flange, bottom fitted.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC. Capped girder shop sequence: weld and UT the bearing stiffener CJPs and any under-flange attachments, check the top flange flatness, then fit and weld the cap.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
